lead: Things a person owns as files, account items or registered tokens: fonts, creative assets, game and platform items, personal media files, domains and NFTs, organised by type, then archetype (typeface, skin line, collection) with file formats and titles kept out of the tree as attributes.

b.v: open file without locks > personalised watermark > locked to an account > licence in a locker
b.w: You own it only if it is not locked; ownership ranks above catalogue size.

depts.note: Organised by type classification (Vox-ATypI / Linotype style groups); foundries go in the brand register.

b.v: desktop, web, app, server (a fit, not a ladder)
b.w: The same family is licensed separately per use.
Character set decides where it can be used.

b.v: variable font > full static family > few weights
b.w: More weights and widths give more range.

s.brief: Split the single 'Digital font' kind into classification kinds. Archetypes are classic typeface families (e.g. Garamond, Caslon, Baskerville, Bodoni, Times New Roman, Helvetica, Futura, Gill Sans, Univers, Frutiger, Akzidenz-Grotesk, Gotham, Rockwell, Clarendon, Courier, Fraktur, Noto, Roboto, Inter) with originating designer/foundry as mk, year, and versions = notable digital revivals/releases (e.g. Adobe Garamond, Garamond Premier, EB Garamond; Neue Haas Grotesk / Helvetica Now). Detail: weights, widths, optical sizes, variable axes, scripts. Keep existing Google/Canada Type/etc. families as versions or m where they fit. Build a foundry brand register (Monotype, Linotype, Adobe, Hoefler&Co, Commercial Type, Klim, Dalton Maag, Grilli Type, Colophon, Emigre, Font Bureau, House Industries, Canada Type, Cadson Demak, Google Fonts, Mark Simonson Studio, Typotheque, Morisawa). Licence scope and 'variable' are types, not kinds.

k.brief: Grotesque, neo-grotesque, geometric, humanist as types.
Old-style, transitional, didone as types.
CJK, Arabic, Devanagari, Thai etc. as types; Noto as a pan-script archetype.
Dingbats such as Zapf Dingbats, Font Awesome, Material Symbols.

depts.note: Files bought or downloaded to make other work; tier at the generic end, variety where communities collect (sample libraries, 3D printing, AI models).

b.v: commercial use allowed > personal use only
b.w: Decides what you may make with it.
Format and host program must match.

s.brief: Restraint: drop single-shop SKUs (Simple co, Ilana Griffo, Design Panoply, ArtsyGet listings) unless they are a recognised icon; keep a few market-covering marketplaces as ranges only if useful (Creative Market, Envato Elements, Adobe Stock). Merge 'Other design templates' into one Design template kind with types (social media, presentation, CV, print, mockup). Add stock photo/illustration and icon set kinds. Presets: photo presets (Lightroom presets, film-emulation packs such as VSCO, RNI as archetypes if sourced) and LUTs (CUBE format, film-emulation LUTs) with formats as types.

k.brief: Types: social media, presentation, CV, print, mockup, website theme file.
Types by host: Procreate, Photoshop ABR, Krita.
Types: After Effects, Premiere Pro MOGRT, DaVinci Resolve, Final Cut.

s.brief: Downloadable patterns for crafts. Archetypes are famous named patterns or pattern lines with their designer/publisher (e.g. widely knitted Ravelry patterns, indie sewing-pattern houses' signature patterns, Big 4 PDF lines). Add cross-stitch and embroidery chart and 3D-printing file kinds only if not better covered under 3D; keep 3D-printable models on the 3D shelf.

k.brief: Includes machine-embroidery files (PES, DST) as types.
SVG cut files for Cricut/Silhouette, printable papercraft.

s.brief: Archetypes: icon assets and reference sets (e.g. Utah teapot, Stanford bunny as reference models; Poly Haven HDRIs/materials; Quixel Megascans; VRChat avatar bases such as popular base bodies, if sourced). 3D printing: notable printable models (3DBenchy as reference test print, Articulated dragons etc.) sourced from Printables/Thingiverse/Wikipedia. Formats (STL, OBJ, FBX, glTF, USD, 3MF) are types. Drop the single RenderHub SKU unless it fits an archetype.

k.brief: Types by format; character/prop/scene as types.
STL/3MF files; 3DBenchy as reference archetype.
Social-VR and VTuber avatars (VRChat, VRM, Live2D).

s.brief: Variety at the enthusiast end. Archetypes: landmark sample libraries and instrument libraries (e.g. Spitfire BBC Symphony Orchestra / LABS, Native Instruments Kontakt libraries, Vienna Symphonic Library, EastWest Symphonic Orchestra, Splice sample packs, Sample Magic, Loopmasters), General MIDI as the MIDI reference, famous synth soundsets. Cut the Sample Magic genre-pack SKU list and the Jacob's Piano titled MIDI bundles (titles out) to at most a range each. Formats (WAV, REX, Kontakt NKI, SFZ, SoundFont) as types. Build brand entries for the main makers.

k.brief: Loops and one-shots.
Sampled orchestral, piano, drum libraries for Kontakt etc.
Soundbanks for Serum, Vital, Massive etc.
Titled song MIDIs are titles: keep as type, no title list.

s.brief: Open-weight model files a person downloads and runs. Archetypes are model families with maker and year (e.g. Llama, Mistral 7B, Gemma, Qwen, DeepSeek; Stable Diffusion 1.5/SDXL, Flux; Whisper) and versions by release. Formats (safetensors, GGUF) and quantisation are types/detail.

depts.note: Items held in a game or platform account; organised by item type, then archetype (skin line or finish), never by SKU.

b.v: platform's own ladder, e.g. CS2 Consumer > Industrial > Mil-Spec > Restricted > Classified > Covert > Contraband
tradable on open market > tradable in-platform > account-bound
b.w: Decides whether it has resale value.

b.v: CS2 wear: Factory New > Minimal Wear > Field-Tested > Well-Worn > Battle-Scarred
b.w: Float and pattern index drive collector value.

s.brief: Replace the long Riot/Valve SKU lists with archetypes: skin lines and finishes that recur across weapons (CS2: Dragon Lore, Howl, Asiimov, Fade, Doppler, Case Hardened, Crimson Web, Hyper Beast, Medusa; Valorant bundles: Prime, Reaver, Elderflame, Oni, Glitchpop, RGX 11z Pro, Kuronami). Versions = weapons the line appears on, 2.0 revisions; detail = wear, float, pattern, StatTrak/Souvenir. Collection names in r may stay as a short range. Add CS2 gloves as its own kind (moved from Avatar accessory models). Fortnite pickaxes/gliders and Rocket League car items as archetypes where sourced. Brand register: Valve, Riot Games, Epic Games, Psyonix.

k.brief: Knife models (Karambit, Butterfly, M9 Bayonet) as archetypes; finishes as versions/detail.
Take the CS2 glove models from Avatar accessory.
Rocket League car bodies, wheels, decals.

s.brief: Archetypes: iconic outfits and lines (Fortnite Renegade Raider, Galaxy, Black Knight, Skull Trooper; CS2 agents by faction; League of Legends skin lines such as PROJECT, Star Guardian; Dota 2 arcanas; Roblox limiteds such as Dominus; World of Warcraft rare mounts). Trim the CS2 agent SKU list to archetypes. Add mount and housing-decor kinds.

k.brief: Back bling, hats, limited accessories; CS2 gloves go to Glove skin.
Ridable creatures and vehicles in MMOs (WoW, FFXIV).
Furniture for player homes (Animal Crossing, FFXIV housing, Second Life).

s.brief: Titles OUT: drop the titled CS2 music-kit list (keep the kind, at most the publisher range); music kits are a type of item, not a music catalogue. Sticker and patch lists become archetypes by type (tournament/autograph stickers, holo/foil/gold, patches, charms). Merge 'Sticker capsule' contents logic into Containers shelf. Sprays: graffiti and Fortnite sprays as types.

Merge Sticker capsule into the loot-container kind as a type. Archetypes: container series (CS:GO Weapon Case 2013 as originator, operation cases, Chroma/Gamma/Prisma series, sticker capsules, tournament souvenir packages; TF2 Mann Co. crates; Overwatch loot boxes) with versions by number. Cut the 42-case SKU list to series.

Steam community items, Discord/Xbox/PlayStation profile items, messaging stickers (LINE, Telegram, WhatsApp). Archetypes only where a community collects (Steam trading-card sets, foil cards, Steam badges; LINE Friends sticker sets). Merge Profile avatar and Avatar frame into one kind with types.

depts.note: Books, music, video and photos held as files or locker entitlements; formats are types, never models; titles live in the entertainment taxonomies.

b.v: open file without locks > personalised watermark > locked to an account > licence in a locker
b.w: You own it only if it is not locked.

b.v: lossless 24-bit/192 kHz > 24/96 > 16/44.1 > lossy 320 kbps > V0 > 128 kbps
b.w: A measured quality, not a grade.
A measured quality, not a grade.
First for audiobooks; narration judged in the Audie categories.

s.brief: Turn format lists into types (EPUB, Kindle KF8/KFX, PDF, DjVu, FB2, MOBI; CBZ/CBR for comics); drop maker-as-SKU models. Merge 'Text or word-processor file' into E-book as a 'plain text / word-processor' type.
No titles. Formats as types (FLAC, ALAC, WAV, DSD, MP3, AAC; MP4, MKV; locker entitlement). Keep definitions; trim the FLAC model.

Merge the compression-only kinds: camera raw, lossy (JPEG, HEIC, WebP, AVIF) and lossless (PNG, TIFF, GIF) become types of one Digital photo or image kind; raw formats per camera maker become type detail, not models. Merge layered and vector files into one Editable graphics file kind with types.

depts.note: Registered names and blockchain tokens; tier for domains, variety for NFT collections.

b.w: Where the artwork is stored decides permanence.

s.brief: Keep the three ending types as t; trim registry models to ~10 representative TLDs (.com, .net, .org, .uk, .de, .io, .ai, .app, .co, .eu) keeping only those already in the data plus well-known ones in old data; drop institutional-only endings (.edu, .aero, .bank, .coop) to a note.

Split the flat NFT list by type with archetypes (collection or series) sourced from Wikipedia/Wikidata/Art Blocks/OpenSea pages: generative art (Chromie Squiggle, Fidenza, Autoglyphs, Terraforms), PFP collections (CryptoPunks as originator, Bored Ape Yacht Club, Azuki, Pudgy Penguins, Moonbirds, Doodles, Meebits), Bitcoin Ordinals (NodeMonkes, Taproot Wizards), game items, virtual land (Decentraland, The Sandbox, Otherside), blockchain names (ENS .eth). Unique vs multi-edition stays as types. Long-tail unsourced collections drop.

k.brief: ENS .eth and similar names held as tokens.
